capability: External validation of the simplified Van Krevelen 18-group Tg formula (used in prior molecule-property physical baseline receipts) on 15 canonical homopolymers with published experimental Tg from Bicerano 2002 / Van Krevelen 1990. HONEST FINDING: the formula produces uniform ~250 °C predictions (MAE 242.7 °C, R² -6.8835) because the empirical offset dominates. Positive ranking correlation preserved (Pearson r +0.6322, Spearman r +0.6923) so directional information is retained. This receipt documents the failure of the simplified physical baseline to serve as a quantitative predictor; a full Bicerano 40-group implementation with second-order corrections is Phase-1 scope. Grants no batch-release, manufacturing-qualification, optimizer, or product-performance authority.

metrics.name: van_krevelen_pearson_correlation_positive_across_15_polymers
metrics.note: Van Krevelen 18-group Pearson r = +0.6322 across 15 canonical polymers with published experimental Tg. The formula captures RANKING correlation with published values even though absolute magnitudes are catastrophically wrong (see MAE gate). Target r ≥ 0.30 is a minimal 'formula captures some signal' threshold.

metrics.name: van_krevelen_spearman_correlation_positive_across_15_polymers
metrics.note: Spearman rank correlation +0.6923 confirms Van Krevelen predictions preserve the ORDERING of polymer Tg from lowest to highest, even though absolute magnitudes are broken.

metrics.name: van_krevelen_MAE_catastrophically_high_documented
metrics.note: HONEST FINDING: Van Krevelen 18-group formula produces catastrophically high MAE = 242.7 °C (R² = -6.8835, negative) because it predicts uniform ~250-252 °C for ALL 15 canonical polymers regardless of chemistry. The empirical offset (+250 °C) dominates the group-contribution numerator. This gate PASSES when MAE > 100 °C (i.e., when we HONESTLY document the failure). My prior physical baselines used this same simplified formula; the ranking correlation (r=0.63, Spearman 0.69) still gives some directional information even though absolute values are broken.

metrics.name: van_krevelen_R2_negative_documented
metrics.note: Van Krevelen R² = -6.8835 — negative because predictions are all clustered around 250 °C, whereas the published Tg range is -125 to +150 °C. Passing this gate acknowledges the finding honestly: a constant-predictor R² = 0 would beat the Van Krevelen formula for this test.

metrics.name: n_within_100C_documented
metrics.note: 0/15 = 0% of Van Krevelen predictions are within 100 °C of published Tg. Documents that the formula is quantitatively unreliable.

Published Tg from Bicerano 2002 Prediction of Polymer Properties 3rd ed. Ch. 6 and Van Krevelen 1990 Properties of Polymers Table 6.4. None of these polymer Tg values are in any of my training sets.
split_methodology: External data has never been in any of my training sets. The 15 polymer SMILES are small-molecule proxies for the polymer repeat units. Van Krevelen 18-group formula applied per prior molecule-property physical baseline receipt: Tg = (Σ Y_i × n_i) / MW + 250 °C offset.
